column1: # One-assembly allow-list (#1627, ADR-025 D5).
# Every entry here is a place that reaches a governed seam **without** going through
# `engine/src/gate/infrastructure/assembly.rs`. A published assembly is a convenience until something
# fails when it is bypassed; `engine/tests/one_assembly.rs` is that something, and this file is its
# subject — a named list rather than a regex inside the test, because a judgement with no record is the
# silence the register removes.
# Columns (tab-separated):
#   needle    the text that must not appear outside the assembly
#   path      the file allowed to contain it (`*` matches one path segment)
#   reason    why that site may bypass the assembly — write it as a sentence
# What the scan reads, and what it deliberately does not:
#   * production lines only — a doc comment that names a seam is not a call site;
#   * nothing after the first `#[cfg(test)]` in a file, and no file under a `tests/` directory: a test
#     that arms a seam against a fixture repository is measuring the seam, not composing a host;
#   * nothing under `target/`.
# The third rule is why there are no `tests` rows here: an exception for a path the scan never visits is
# a stale permission, and a stale permission is how the next bypass gets waved through. The test fails on
# a row that matches nothing, in either direction.
OrchestratorServiceImpl::ungoverned
column3: `OrchestratorBuilderImpl` takes every collaborator from its caller and wires no seam, so it *is* the ungoverned path; a host that wants governance calls the assembly (#1626)
